sources.title: FIDE Laws of Chess (effective 1 January 2023)
sources.why_it_matters: Primary source for move legality, castling, en passant, repetition, checkmate, stalemate, dead position, and 75-move/fivefold rules.

sources.title: Portable Game Notation Specification and Implementation Guide
sources.why_it_matters: Canonical specification for FEN/PGN field semantics: active color, castling availability, EP target square, halfmove clock, and fullmove number.

sources.title: python-chess core documentation
sources.why_it_matters: Clear reference implementation documentation for legal vs pseudo-legal moves, board validity, mirror transforms, and API semantics.

sources.title: python-chess source (status()/is_valid())
sources.why_it_matters: Concrete import-time status taxonomy: bad castling rights, invalid EP square, opposite check, too many checkers, impossible check, and more.

sources.title: Stockfish position.cpp
sources.why_it_matters: Production-grade reference for internal state validation, EP sanitization, castling-right consistency, hash recomputation, and legal move edge cases.

sources.title: Stockfish Docs: UCI & Commands
sources.why_it_matters: Official divide/perft example and operational guidance useful for test harnesses.

sources.title: Chessprogramming Wiki: Perft
sources.why_it_matters: Explains why perft/divide is the standard debugging oracle for move generation and make/unmake.

sources.title: Chessprogramming Wiki: Perft Results
sources.why_it_matters: Provides standard reference positions and node counts used across engine debugging.

sources.title: Daniel Gourion, An upper bound for the number of chess diagrams without promotion
sources.why_it_matters: Useful for the legal-diagram/reachability distinction and for retrograde-style pawn/promotion reasoning.

sources.title: Brunner et al., Complexity of Retrograde and Helpmate Chess Problems
sources.why_it_matters: Puts formal weight behind the claim that reachability is a genuinely harder problem than local move legality.

sources.title: Méndez et al., Metamorphic testing of chess engines
sources.why_it_matters: Introduces metamorphic relations as a practical testing aid in the oracle-poor parts of engine validation.

sources.title: Martin et al., Re-evaluating metamorphic testing of chess engines: A replication study
sources.why_it_matters: Important caution: metamorphic evaluation discrepancies can come from implementation details rather than true bugs.

sources.title: python-chess Syzygy endgame tablebase probing
sources.why_it_matters: Exact WDL/DTZ oracle for many small endgames, with the important caveat that castling-right positions are excluded.
